_schema.id: stable entry id: imp-<stratum-or-sector-slug>-<seller-slug-or-marketwide>-<yyyy[mm]>; the month is included only at verified granularity (yyyy alone until the effective month is byte-verified); a sector slug substitutes where the stratum assignment is pending an owner ruling; ids are immutable once committed even if verification later refines the date, stratum, or seller (stability beats pattern purity; the refinement is logged in the entry)
_schema.stratum: CPI item stratum per docs/rx-100-tier-map.md naming (needs_verification flags travel with the name until the owner's stratum-list pull)
_schema.tier: corridor tier of the stratum at entry time: R | A | B | null (pending owner ruling — corridor_use must then state both branches)
_schema.seller: firm, or 'industry-wide' with the aggregation basis stated in the entry
_schema.improvement: what got better, one sentence — dated, seller-attributable, menu-adjacent (posted inclusion added / named fee eliminated or reduced / dominating tier introduced); diffuse quality drift and hedonic judgments are NOT registrable
_schema.link_year: the link year containing the effective date (codebook §6 applied symmetrically); an improvement feeds that link year's I_i ONLY. Entries whose link years precede the corridor's first computed link can never feed live I_i arithmetic and are marked corridor-dead: machinery demonstration / A-Q evidence only
_schema.improvement_type: re-bundling | fee-elimination | fee-reduction | quality-add | dominating-tier-introduction | access-expansion
_schema.monetization_route: codebook §5 route hierarchy run in reverse: named-fee-eliminated | a-la-carte-removed | tier-delta-compressed; the route caps the magnitude exactly as it caps degradations; n/a for cross-reference/non-event entries
_schema.superset_route_flag: true when only a superset-style route prices the improvement — the interval-and-flag discipline, mirroring the ledger's superset_flag: the magnitude publishes as an interval with the point at the route's cap, flagged, never as a bare point; null until the monetization route is ruled
_schema.magnitude: monetized annual I contribution with derivation and provenance tag (data/incidence-proxies.md pattern); null until owner-verified — unverified magnitudes are never asserted; NEVER netted against degradations
_schema.incidence: utilization share with provenance tag per codebook §8 rules; the published [0%,100%] interval where no usable seller-specific source exists. Role pinned: magnitudes enter I_i incidence-weighted, exactly as M_i events weight (codebook §8) — the bound formula's I_i is the incidence-weighted sum
_schema.corridor_use: Tier B: feeds the entry's link-year I_i in the stratum bound [-I_i/E_i, +M_i/E_i] (moves L). Tier R: zero I_i in ALL cases — where the improvement creates a cheaper weakly-dominating path or eliminates/reduces a named fee it prints through codebook §4 negative-event grammar in the Inclusion Ledger (ledger_crossref required once the event exists); where it is irrelevant to every frozen vector it is a §4 NON-event and ledger_crossref stays null with the non-event ruling cited — compliant by rule. Tier A: strata are unmeasured, no Inclusion-Ledger path exists — A-Q evidence only, zero I_i. Tier null: both candidate branches stated pending the owner ruling
_schema.ledger_crossref: ledger event id in data/ledger-events.json where the same fact is a ledger negative event; null where no event exists — including permanently, by rule, for Tier-R frozen-vector non-events (ruling cited in corridor_use)
_schema.materiality: pass/fail against the shared numeric de-minimis floor — ONE number governing both registers' corridor arithmetic (it gates M_i and I_i entry; the Exclusion census itself stays floor-free for observability), whose first existence is this register's binding G4 commit (never stated in design docs — first-existence discipline); null until the floor exists
_schema.verified: date of last owner byte-verification; null for candidates
_schema.evidence_capture: snapshot manifest hash or capture.py --manual registration + seller's own document + >=1 independent corroboration (codebook §12 format parity with the Exclusion Register); null until captured — open capture tasks go in owner_tasks, never here
_schema.owner_tasks: open owner actions for the entry (captures to run, rulings to make, facts to byte-verify); never a substitute for the evidence fields
_schema.sources: primary or strongest available; full evidence in the archive

_rules: Structure mirrors data/ledger-events.json's _schema-plus-array pattern with these stated deviations: the array key is 'entries' (ledger: 'events'); added fields link_year, tier, corridor_use, superset_route_flag, materiality, owner_tasks; extended status enum. The mirror claim is scoped to the pattern, not field-for-field.

Inclusion requires ALL of: documented-and-dated (T1 in reverse), menu-adjacent, monetizable by the reverse route hierarchy, above the shared materiality floor (one number for both registers' corridor arithmetic, set only in this register's binding G4 commit — no Exclusion-side floor exists before that commit, and the Exclusion census stays floor-free).

Link-year scoping: an improvement belongs to exactly the link year containing its effective date (codebook §6 applied symmetrically) and feeds that link year's I_i only; entries whose link years precede the corridor's first computed link are corridor-dead (A-Q evidence / machinery demonstration).
No netting: I_i and M_i are separate sums, published separately; improvements never offset degradations within an entry or a stratum line.

No double-counting, split by tier: Tier R improvements print through codebook §4 negative-event grammar ONLY where a cheaper weakly-dominating path or named-fee elimination exists (crossref required once the event exists); Tier R improvements irrelevant to every frozen vector are §4 non-events (crossref null by rule, ruling cited); Tier A strata have no Inclusion-Ledger path — A-Q evidence only. Zero I_i in every non-B case.

Evidence FORMAT bar is identical to the Exclusion Register's (codebook §12); admissibility is deliberately stricter (menu-adjacency, reverse-route monetizability) — the residual assumption this creates is named in docs/rx-100-audit-protocols.md §7 as the A-Q residual clause and proposed for the proposal §3 ladder with a sensitivity row.
Rejection log: every candidate rejected at the menu-adjacency or monetizability test is logged with its reason, and the rejection log publishes as a public artifact.

Symmetric bounty, extended: a third party documenting a missed improvement is an A-Q hit handled by the correction protocol, exactly as a missed degradation is an A-R hit — and a third party defensibly monetizing a REJECTED candidate is an A-Q hit too (a rejected candidate was not 'missed'; without this extension it would escape the bounty by construction).
No entry below status 'verified-preprint' may appear in any public artifact; 'candidate' entries exist only to queue owner verification.
